title: Semantic-Constrained Generative Modeling for Health-Care Data Under Distribution Shift
content: Generative models have become increasingly important for synthetic healthcare data generation, yet they often prioritize statistical fidelity while overlooking clinically meaningful semantic relationships, particularly under distribution shift. This study proposes a Semantic-Constrained Variational Autoencoder (SC-VAE) that integrates ontology-inspired clinical constraints into deep generative modelling to improve the semantic plausibility of synthetic critical care data. The framework was evaluated using harmonized MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV intensive care unit datasets under temporal and cross-version distribution shift and compared with conventional Variational Autoencoder (VAE), Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), and Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) baselines. Model performance was assessed using complementary statistical and semantic metrics, including Maximum Mean Discrepancy, precision, recall, coverage, Rule Satisfaction Rate, Semantic Validity Score, and robustness under increasing distribution shift. The results show that SC-VAE achieved the highest overall semantic rule satisfaction while maintaining competitive statistical fidelity, whereas DDPM provided the strongest distributional matching and feature coverage. However, strict record-level semantic validity remained low across all models, indicating that improved aggregate rule compliance does not necessarily imply complete semantic consistency for individual synthetic records. These findings demonstrate that statistical fidelity and semantic validity represent complementary objectives and suggest that integrating semantic constraints into generative models provides a practical approach for improving the trustworthiness of synthetic healthcare data under distribution shift.
